turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, come through. You can keep him on your lap. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's his right ear, doctor. He's been screaming at night, and it came on after a cold. I don't know, the days are blurring.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): My ear is sore.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame, Leo. Which ear is it?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): This one. The right.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right ear. Is the crying mostly at night?
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, nights are the worst. He'll fall asleep and then wake up crying. Daytime he still plays, he's just grumpy.
[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Sorry to jump in. I'm his gogo, I live in with them. It was three nights, not two. I was up walking with him.
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three? I thought it was two. Um, well, actually I was on a late shift so I wasn't there the first night, maybe three, I don't know.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): So about two to three nights, we won't force an exact start. Is the cold still hanging on?
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The runny nose was last week and that's mostly gone. There's still a bit of a dry cough, not all the time.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has he felt hot at all? Any fever?
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No fever. I've felt him, he's not hot.
[SEG0014] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He was hot, doctor. Last night his forehead was burning. I said so.
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't think that was a fever. He was under the fleece blanket, crying, so of course he felt warm.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's okay. Did either of you get a thermometer on him, an actual number?
[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Ours packed up and I haven't bought another. So there's no number.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pus or fluid leaking from the ear? Does he pull at it?
[SEG0020] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No discharge, nothing. He pulls the right ear and then he starts crying.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting, runny tummy, or a rash on him at the moment?
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, no diarrhoea, no rash now. Appetite is down, he left half his porridge. He's drinking, water and some juice.
[SEG0023] person_4 (CAREGIVER): That apple juice he likes. We nearly didn't make it, the robot by the garage was out and the queue was shocking.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, that corner is always a mess. What have you given him for the pain?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panado, the strawberry syrup, last night and this morning. Maybe five mils, I'm not a hundred percent sure, it might have been a bit less. No ear drops.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Was that only twice, or on a schedule through the day?
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just when he cried. Twice, I think. Not timed properly.
[SEG0028] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I gave him a spoon of the purple cough mixture as well, the bottle from the pharmacy. I don't know the name. It was for the cough.
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And before you ask, my sister takes biotin gummies every morning for her hair and she keeps offering them. I didn't give him any, that's hers.
[SEG0030] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I should say, I take a water tablet, the little white one, for my blood pressure. I didn't give him that either.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Glad you checked. Has he ever had antibiotics, or a reaction to a medicine?

[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, long ago he had amoxicillin, the pink one I think, and he got a rash, maybe. I'm not sure it was even from that. I can't remember when, it was ages ago, sometime before he was two. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): A possible rash with the amoxicillin, but you're not sure, and there's no date. Anything else, foods?
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that I know of. No food allergies. Gogo, did you see that rash?
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I wasn't with them then, so I can't say yes or no. His dad has sugar, diabetes, he takes metformin. That's the father, not Leo.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has Leo had ear trouble before? Operations, grommets?
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One sore ear last winter, it settled on its own. No operations, no grommets. Otherwise he's well. He does crèche three mornings a week.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Who's at home day to day?
[SEG0039] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Me and gogo. His dad is away on the mines most weeks. Nobody smokes in the house.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leo, I need to look in the ears with a small light. I'll go slowly.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. It's sore.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): The right eardrum is red and a little bulging. The left one looks clear, no redness. His throat is mildly red, the chest is clear, and the neck is soft with no stiffness.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Temperature is 36.9. Heart rate 118, which fits a cross little boy. He's not feverish while he's sitting here.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is an early middle ear infection after the cold. He's not particularly unwell and we haven't actually measured a fever, so I'd rather watch and wait than start an antibiotic today.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing at all? He screamed half the night. I felt a bit hopeless, hey.

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Carry on with the Panado. For his size, strawberry syrup, 7.5 mils of the 120 milligram in 5 mils, up to four times a day, properly spaced, not only once the screaming has started. Leave that purple cough mixture alone, we don't know what it is. And nobody else's pills.

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he's not better in two days, bring him back. Same if a real fever shows up or the pain gets much worse, don't wait the two days, and then we'll start an antibiotic that isn't amoxicillin, because of that possible rash. No script to fetch today. If he's playing and drinking, crèche is alright; if he's miserable, keep him home.

Panado had been given last night and again this morning, only twice in total, not on a proper schedule.
Possible amoxicillin rash occurred long ago, sometime before he was two years old.
Past history: one previous sore ear last winter that settled on its own.
He attends crèche three mornings a week.
Left ear exam was clear, with no redness.
Neck exam finding was 'soft with no stiffness', not just absence of stiffness.
Doctor stated he was not feverish while in clinic.
Plan was watch-and-wait rather than starting an antibiotic today.
No prescription was issued today ('No script to fetch today').
